To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) critical slowing-down is the phenomenon of slowing and simultaneous amplifying fluctuations of the system variables near bifurcation points, (2) the phenomenon is generic and is present for any co-dimension 2 bifurcation, and (3) the phenomenon is present in the stochastic dynamics of a power system near bifurcations of global stability.
the phenomenon of critical slowing down is a generic feature of systems close to the loss of global asymptotic stability.

the phenomenon of critical slowing down can be observed from single-node autostructure of system state variables, that it is a good indicator of the proximity to the loss of global system stability, and that it is possible to derive analytical expressions for the correlation functions of system state vector fluctuations in terms of the system eigenvalues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental question of how to detect and quantify the proximity to the threshold of the global instability of the power system.
the analysis of stochastic dynamics of power systems in the vicinity of saddle-node bifurcations.
the analysis of critical fluctuations of the state variables of a power system close to the threshold of loss of stability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the onset of the critical slowing-down phenomenon is an unambiguous marker of the proximity of the loss of global power system stability and can be used to trigger appropriate preventive measures.
the phenomenon of critical slowing down is an important indicator of the proximity of a system to the threshold of a global bifurcation and can be detected by the analysis of single node observables.

the phenomenon of critical slowing down, in particular the amplification of the slowest mode, is a good indicator of the approach of the system to the loss of global (saddle-node) stability, and that it is possible to use this information for the early warning of such a loss of stability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
critical slowing-down is an important phenomenon for power systems and can be detected by simple statistical methods.
the phenomenon of critical slowing- down is a universal indicator of the proximity to the loss of system global stability.
the critical slowing-down phenomenon can serve as an early warning signal of approach to the saddle-node bifucation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
critical slowing-down is an indicator of approach to instability in the vicinity of saddle-node bifurcations.
the phenomenon of critical slowing down can be exploited to detect the onset of voltage collapse and phase angle instability in power systems.

critical slowing-down is an inherent property of the stochastic dynamics of a power system in the immediate vicinity of the threshold of global stability and can be used as a marker of the proximity to this threshold.
